owner_and_capability: People Directory — the caregiver capability leaves services/users (slice 5 of #2728, #3754) for modules/peopledirectory/compose, as decided on 28.09.2026: it stays with People Directory and does not move to Identity & Access. The capability lock and the four blocker reads reach education.group_teacher, education.group_substitution, active.group_supervisors and activities.supervisors only through consumer-owned ports in People Directory vocabulary; the lock already runs through the owner ports of #2727. The audit event of a capability change goes through a consumer-owned port that the root binds to the authentication audit trail.
atomic_cutover: One code-only change. caregiver_capability.go, caregiver_capability_views.go, caregiver_identity.go and the CaregiverCapabilityService interface move to modules/peopledirectory/compose; Enable and Disable are split into named steps so the moved code fits the module function-length and complexity ratchets. The two typed refusals (CaregiverCapabilityBlockedError, AccountNotAssignedToTenantError) move into models/users beside CaregiverCapabilityState, so the suites keep asserting on them without a new key. The ports that named models/audit, models/activities and modules/studentpresence are replaced by consumer-owned ports in models/users vocabulary: CaregiverCapabilityAudit is bound in services to the authentication audit trail with the same event types and metadata, SupervisionBlockers and PlannedSupervisionBlockers are bound by database/repositories adapters over the same Student Presence and Timetable repositories with the same errors. The unused DB dependency is dropped. The policy rule people-directory.application.student-presence-public allows no import any more and is removed. The services/users suites stay where they are, because every other test scope would add keys; the views suite drives the moved views through their exported constructor. Routes, error bodies and /api/iot error texts are unchanged.
